items.reason: The `run:`-interpolation half was already mechanical (check-actions' run-injection rule plus a whole-tree fixture); the residual half — an untrusted value correctly passed through `env:` and then expanded UNQUOTED by the shell — was not, so I added the `unquoted-untrusted-env` blocking rule and mutation fixtures that reintroduce the real bug into both write-path workflows and require the check to go red.

Extracted the ratchet protocol (verdict ladder, report, flags, exit codes, the no-op --tighten rule) into scripts/lint/ratchet.mjs, rebuilt both ratchets on it so each keeps only its debt format and its measurement, and pinned in a fixture that the two diverge in exactly one place (`zero` = `dead` for ruff, `burnt-down` for TypeScript).

Added a keyless deterministic injection eval: 13 hostile issue bodies each paired with the plan an OBEDIENT model would return, asserting the guard refuses it by name before anything is written; building it found and fixed two real weaknesses (the untrusted-input label rode in round 1 only, and the fence around the issue text was one the issue text could close).

The first cold-clone failure (typecheck -> schemas:gen -> Python) now diagnoses itself through scripts/schemas-gen.mjs instead of dying as a generic npm error, AGENTS.md states the prerequisite, and a nightly cold-clone workflow runs the three documented commands from an empty checkout with no caches and opens an issue when they fail; I could not execute that run from this session, so the workflow's first real verdict comes from CI.

lessons: This repository answers scanner findings in file headers rather than in checks, and the headers are usually right — so the useful work is rarely 'fix the finding', it is 'find the half of the argument the header asserts and no gate covers'. Here that was `env:` passing being treated as sufficient when quoting at the read site is the other half.

A safety property argued in a comment is worth converting into a MUTATION test, not just a passing assertion: reintroduce the real bug into the real file and require the check to go red, with a loud failure when the mutation stops matching. A tree-wide 'no findings' assertion passes identically whether the detector works or is broken.

When two scripts implement one concept twice, the shared part is usually the verdict ladder and the CLI, not the parsing — and the one place they legitimately disagree is worth naming after the MEASUREMENT rather than the verdict, so each side can map it to its own answer without a flag.

Writing an adversarial fixture is a cheap way to find real hardening: simulating an obedient model against a hostile prompt surfaced that the untrusted-input label only rode in the round that reads, not the round that writes code.
